text: Mizkif, also known as Matthew Rinaudo, is an American Twitch streamer and YouTuber born on February 16, and raised in Montclair, New Jersey. He is of Italian descent and founded the gaming organization One True King. Mizkif began streaming in 2016 and gained popularity in 2018 as a cameraman for fellow streamer Paul "Ice Poseidon" Denino. On April 30, 2019, he and Esfand were banned for making an insensitive joke toward streamer and cosplayer Jenna "Meowri" during a livestream at PAX East, though they were unbanned seven days later. In March 2020, Mizkif earned over $5,600 during a sleeping stream, describing it as a relaxing break from his usual gaming routine. He was the third-most-watched Twitch streamer during the 2020 U.S. presidential election, behind Trainwreckstv and HasanAbi. On October 11, 2020, Mizkif, along with Asmongold, Esfand, Rich Campbell, and Tips Out, announced the launch of One True King. He reached one million Twitch followers on January 18, 2021. In October 2021, he appeared in the Twitch leaks, where he was ranked 23rd with a reported payout of $2,086,548.21 from August 2019 to October 2021. On March 2022, he won Best Just Chatting Streamer at the 2021 Streamer Awards and was also nominated for Streamer of the Year. On September 19, 2022, he was accused by Trainwreckstv of downplaying a sexual assault incident involving his roommate CrazySlick and female streamer AdrianahLee, and the following day, Ice Poseidon published comments from Mizkif between 2018 and 2019 deemed racist and homophobic. As a result, Mizkif was placed on leave by One True King, though a Texas-based law firm, Jackson Walker, found no direct evidence that he attempted to cover up the assault, and his membership was later reinstated. On January 2, 2023, Mizkif uploaded a video apologizing for "insensitive" and "tone-deaf" behavior in an October 2022 broadcast. On January 13, 2023, he was banned from Twitch for watching banned content named "Grossgore," and was unbanned less than 24 hours later. On February 7, 2023, he was banned for violating the DMCA after watching the reality TV series MILF Manor, and was unbanned the next day. On May 28, 2023, he announced joining Rumble, a video hosting platform, to stream some content there. On October 25, 2025, cosplayer and streamer Emiru accused Mizkif of misconduct, including unwanted physical contact, emotional abuse, and stalking, stating they were in a relationship for several years that ended in 2024, and that Mizkif threatened retaliation if she spoke about it; Mizkif denied the more serious allegations and disputed parts of her account. In response, One True King disclosed on Twitter on October 27, 2025, that Mizkif had been terminated for unrelated reasons "some time ago" and holds no stake in the organization or its affiliated companies. In 2021, Mizkif announced plans to develop a platform game titled Unrooted, influenced by Jump King, which was showcased at the 2022 OTK Games Expo and officially released on Steam on August 2, 2024. On January 17, 2024, he opened Iron Forge Gym in Austin, Texas, co-owned with Norwegian streamer Knut, offering weight lifting, MMA, and wrestling classes. On May 6, 2024, he launched the "Just Chatting Podcast," a weekly podcast where he interviews guests one-on-one. On December 21, 2019, he held a charity stream for St. David's Children's Hospital in Austin, Texas, raising over $5,000 to purchase toys for patients. In June 2021, he and fellow streamer Ryan "Simply" Reeves rappelled down 600 Congress, a 32-story building in Austin, for a Make-A-Wish fundraiser titled "Over the Edge," raising over $20,000. On February 10, 2023, he held a 26-hour charity stream to support victims of the 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquakes, raising $80,799. Mizkif began dating wildlife rehabilitator Maya Higa in 2019 and announced their breakup on September 14, 2021. He has a heart condition known as viral myocarditis and has publicly discussed his struggles with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). In early June 2021, he purchased an Audi R8, which sustained $100,000 in damages after being hit in a parking lot on January 3, 2022.
